Faith is the substance of what we hope for
and the evidence of things unseen.
This seems to me its essential nature."

7.speaker: narrator
7.text: Then I heard:

7.speaker: st_peter
7.text:
"You understand correctly,
if you grasp why he placed Faith
among substances and then among evidences."

9.speaker: narrator
9.text: Then I heard:

9.speaker: st_peter
9.text:
"If everything learned
in the world below through teaching
were understood this way,
no clever sophistry would find a place."

9.speaker: narrator
9.text:
This was breathed forth from that burning love,
which then added:

9.speaker: st_peter
9.text:
"The composition and weight
of this coin have been thoroughly examined—
but tell me, do you have it in your purse?"

11.speaker: narrator
11.text:
Then from that profound light
shining there came:

11.speaker: st_peter
11.text:
"This precious jewel
on which every virtue is founded—
where did you get it?"

12.speaker: dante
12.text: The great outpouring of the Holy Spirit,

13.speaker: dante
13.text:
I answered, "spread across both
the ancient and new scriptures,
forms a perfect logical proof
that convinced me with such sharpness
that all other demonstrations seem dull."

13.speaker: narrator
13.text: Then I heard:

13.speaker: st_peter
13.text:
"These old and new authorities
that you find so convincing—
why do you accept them as God's word?"

15.speaker: dante
15.text:
I said, "lies in the works that followed,
for which Nature never heated iron
or struck her anvil."

15.speaker: narrator
15.text: The answer came:

15.speaker: st_peter
15.text:
"Tell me, who assures you
that those works ever happened?
Only the thing that needs proving
testifies to itself."

1.speaker: narrator
1.text:
If it should ever happen that this Sacred Poem,
to which both heaven and earth have lent their hand,
this work that has made me lean through many years,
should overcome the cruelty that bars me
from the beautiful sheepfold where I slept as a lamb,
enemy to the wolves that wage war upon it—
then with a different voice, with different fleece,
I will return as poet, and at the font
where I was baptized I will take the laurel crown.
For there I entered into the Faith
that makes all souls known to God,
and for this Faith Peter crowned my brow.
Then toward us moved a light
from that company which gave forth the first fruits
of those Christ left behind as his vicars.
And my Lady, full of ecstasy,
said to me:

1.speaker: beatrice
1.text:
"Look, look! See the Baron
for whom people make pilgrimage to Galicia below."

1.speaker: narrator
1.text:
Just as when a dove settles
near its companion, and both pour forth
their affection, circling and cooing together,
so I saw one great Prince welcomed
by the other with glory,
praising the food that is eaten up there.
But when their greetings were complete,
each stood silent before me,
so blazing bright they overwhelmed my sight.
Then Beatrice smiled and said:

2.speaker: beatrice
2.text:
Illustrious soul, who wrote of the benefactions
of our heavenly court,
make Hope resound at this height.
You know how to embody it,
as Jesus gave the three apostles greater clarity.

7.speaker: beatrice
7.text:
The Church Militant has no child
with greater hope, as is written
in that Sun who illuminates all our company.
Therefore he is granted to come from Egypt
to see Jerusalem
before his warfare on earth is complete.
The other two questions you asked—
not for knowledge but so he may report
how much this virtue pleases you—
I leave to him. He will not find them difficult,
nor cause for boasting. Let him answer,
and may God's grace assist him.

8.speaker: narrator
8.text:
Like a student following his teacher,
ready and eager in his area of expertise
to display his skill,
I said:

8.speaker: dante
8.text:
"Hope is the assured expectation
of future glory, produced by
divine grace and preceding merit.
This light comes to me from many stars,
but he first poured it into my heart
who was the chief singer to the chief captain.
'Let them hope in you,' he says in his high song,
'those who know your name'—and who
with my faith does not know it?
You then instilled me, along with his instilling,
in the Epistle, so that I am full
and rain your rain upon others."

8.speaker: narrator
8.text:
While I spoke, within the living heart
of that fire trembled a radiance,
sudden and frequent, like lightning.
Then it breathed:

8.speaker: st_james
8.text:
"The love with which I burn
toward the virtue that followed me
to the palm and leaving of the field
moves me to speak to you, that you delight
in her. Tell me what Hope promises you."

8.speaker: narrator
8.text: And I:

8.speaker: dante
8.text:
"The old and new Scriptures
set the target, and this reveals to me
all the souls God has made his friends.
Isaiah says each will be clothed
with double garments in his own land—
and his own land is this delightful life.
Your brother too, far more explicitly,
where he writes of the white robes,
reveals this truth to us."

8.speaker: narrator
8.text: First, near the end of these words,

9.speaker: narrator
9.text:
Let them hope in you" was heard above us,
and all the choirs responded.
Then a light among them brightened
so that if Cancer held such a crystal,
winter would have a month of one long day.
As a graceful girl rises, moves, and joins the dance
only to honor the new bride,
not from any fault,
so I saw that brightened splendor
approach the two who revolved in a wheel
befitting their ardent love.
It entered into the song and music there,
and my Lady kept her gaze fixed on them
like a bride, silent and motionless.

9.speaker: beatrice
9.text:
"This is he who lay upon the breast
of our Pelican, and this is he
chosen from the cross for the great office.

10.speaker: narrator
10.text:
So spoke my Lady, but her sight
did not move from attentive watching
before or after these words.
Like someone who strains to glimpse
the sun's eclipse a little,
and by looking becomes blind,
so I became before that final fire
until it spoke:

10.speaker: st_john
10.text:
"Why do you daze yourself
trying to see what does not exist here?
My body is earth in the earth, and will remain
with all the others there until our number
matches the eternal plan.
Only two lights have ascended
to the blessed cloister with both garments—
and this you shall carry back to your world."

10.speaker: narrator
10.text:
At these words the flaming circle
fell quiet, along with the sweet mingling
of sounds made by the threefold breath,
just as oars beating in the water
all stop at a whistle's sound
to escape danger or fatigue.
How disturbed I was in my mind
when I turned to look at Beatrice
and could not see her, though I stood
close beside her in the World of Joy!

1.speaker: narrator
1.text:
While I was struggling with my vision gone dark,
from the blazing flame that had blinded me
came a voice that made me listen closely,

saying:

1.speaker: st_john
1.text:
"While you recover the power
of sight that you've consumed in me,

2.speaker: st_john
2.text:
You have consumed yourself in me—let your speaking now make recompense for that.
Begin then, and tell me what your soul aims toward, and know with certainty
that your sight is bewildered, not destroyed,
because the Lady who guides you through this divine realm
carries in her gaze the same power that Ananias held in his hands.

3.speaker: narrator
3.text: I said:

3.speaker: dante
3.text:
"Whether soon or late, as it pleases her,
let the cure come to these eyes that were doorways
when she entered, bringing the fire I burn with eternally.
The Good that gives contentment to this Court
is the Alpha and Omega of all
the scripture that love reads to me, soft or loud."

3.speaker: narrator
3.text:
The same voice that had taken from me
the terror of that sudden blazing light
stirred my thoughts to speak further,
and said:

3.speaker: st_john
3.text:
"You must sift with a finer mesh—
you must tell me who aimed your bow at such a target."

5.speaker: narrator
5.text: And I heard:

5.speaker: st_john
5.text:
"By human reason
and by the authority that accords with it,
hold God as the highest of all your loves.
But tell me again if you feel other cords
drawing you toward him—proclaim
with how many teeth this love is biting you."

5.speaker: narrator
5.text:
The holy purpose of Christ's Eagle
was not hidden from me—rather I perceived
where he wished to lead my confession.
Therefore I began again:

5.speaker: dante
5.text:
"All those bites
that have the power to turn the heart toward God
have worked together in my love.
The existence of the world and my own existence,
the death he endured so that I might live,
and that which all believers hope for, as I do,
along with the living knowledge I spoke of—
these have drawn me from the sea of perverted love
and placed me on the shore of righteous love.
The leaves with which the Eternal Gardener's
entire garden is adorned, I love them
in proportion to the good he has granted them."

5.speaker: narrator
5.text:
As soon as I finished speaking, the sweetest song
resounded through all heaven, and my Lady
joined the others, singing "Holy, holy, holy!"
And just as someone wakes from sleep at bright light,
as the visual spirit races toward
the splendor passed from layer to layer,
and the sleeper recoils from what he sees,
so unconscious in his sudden waking
until judgment comes to his aid—
so Beatrice chased every speck from my eyes
with the radiance of her own,
which cast light for a thousand miles and more.
I saw better afterward than before,
and in a kind of wonder I asked
about a fourth light I saw with us.
My Lady said:

5.speaker: beatrice
5.text:
"Within those rays
the first soul that the First Power ever created
gazes upon its Maker."

5.speaker: narrator
5.text:
As a branch bends its crown downward
when the wind passes, then lifts up again
by its own nature that inclines it upward,
so I did while she was speaking—
amazed at first, then made bold
by the desire to speak that burned in me.
And I began:

5.speaker: dante
5.text:
"O fruit that was brought forth
mature and alone, O ancient father
to whom every wife is daughter and daughter-in-law,
as devoutly as I can, I beg you
to speak with me. You see my wish,
and I don't voice it, wanting to hear you sooner."

5.speaker: narrator
5.text:
Sometimes a covered animal struggles
so that its movement must be apparent
because the covering follows its motion.
In the same way that first soul
showed me through its wrapping
how joyful it was to give me pleasure.
Then it breathed:

5.speaker: adam
5.text:
"Without your speaking it,
I perceive your desire better
than you know anything most certain to you.
For I see it in the truthful mirror
that makes all things reflections of itself
while nothing can make it a reflection of anything else.
You want to hear how long ago God placed me
in the high garden where this Lady
prepared you for so long a climb,
and how long it delighted my eyes,
and the true cause of the great anger,
and the language I used and made.
Now know, my son: the tasting of the tree
was not in itself the cause of such great exile,
but only the transgression of the boundary.
From the place where your Lady summoned Virgil,
through four thousand three hundred and two revolutions
of the sun, I longed for this assembly.
And I saw the sun return to all the stars
of its path nine hundred and thirty times
while I remained upon the earth.
The language I spoke was already extinct
before Nimrod's people undertook
their impossible work.
For no product of human reason
was ever lasting, since human desire changes
in obedience to the heavens.
That humans speak is natural,
but whether this way or that, nature leaves
to your own choice, as seems best to you.
Before I descended to the infernal anguish,
'El' was the name on earth for the Supreme Good
from whom comes all the joy that wraps around me.
Later he was called 'Eli,' and this is fitting,
for human usage is like a leaf
on a branch—one falls and another comes.
On the mountain that rises highest above the waters
I lived, both innocent and guilty,
from the first hour until the one that follows
the sixth, when the sun changes quadrant."

7.speaker: beatrice
7.text: Cast down your sight and see how far you've turned.

9.speaker: beatrice
9.text:
The nature of the motion that keeps still
the center while all the rest revolves around it
begins here as from its starting point.
In this heaven there is no other place
than in the Divine Mind, where kindles
the love that turns it and the power it rains down.
Light and love embrace it in a circle,
as it embraces all the others,
and only He who encircles it understands that boundary.
Its motion is not measured by another's,
but all the others are measured by this one,
as ten is measured by its half and fifth.
How time can have its roots in such a vessel
and its leaves in all the rest
can now be made clear to you.
O Covetousness, you engulf mortals
so deeply beneath you that none has power
to lift his eyes above your waves!
The will blossoms beautifully in mankind,
but unceasing rain converts
the true plums into rotted fruit.
Faith and innocence are found
only in children—then both take flight
before down covers their cheeks.
One child still lisping observes the fasts
who later, when his tongue is free,
devours any food in any season.
Another child still babbling loves
and obeys his mother,
who when he speaks perfectly
longs to see her buried.
So the white skin grows dark
in the first appearance of fair Dawn,
daughter of him who brings morning and leaves night.
That this may not amaze you,
consider that on earth no one governs—
which is why the human family goes astray.
But before January is completely removed from winter
by that hundredth part neglected on earth,
these celestial circles will roar so loud
that the long-awaited tempest
will spin the ships' sterns where their prows should be,
so the fleet will run its true course
and genuine fruit will follow the flower.

2.speaker: narrator
2.text:
Like someone who sees a candle's flame reflected in a mirror,
lit from behind before they turn to look directly at the source,
then spins around to check if the glass tells the truth,
finding perfect harmony between reflection and reality
like music matching its own rhythm—
so I remember doing as I gazed into those beautiful eyes
that Love had made into snares to capture me.
And when I turned, my own eyes touched
by what appears in that revolving sphere
whenever we focus our intent gaze upon it,
I saw a point radiating light so sharp and piercing
that any sight it kindles must close tight
against such overwhelming brilliance.
Whatever star appears smallest from earth
would seem a moon if placed beside this point,
as close as one star sits next to another.
Perhaps at the distance where a halo appears
to circle the light that paints it
when the mist holding it grows thickest—
at such a distance around the point, a ring of fire
spun so swiftly it would have outpaced
whatever motion fastest girds our world.
This ring was circled by another,
that by a third, the third by a fourth,
the fourth by a fifth, then a sixth around the fifth.
The seventh spread so wide in its circumference
that Juno's rainbow messenger entire
would be too narrow to contain it.
So too the eighth and ninth, and each one
moved more slowly as its number placed it
farther distant from the first.
The ring whose flame burned most crystal-clear
was closest to that stainless spark,
because, I think, it drinks most deeply of its truth.
My Lady, seeing me bewildered and perplexed,
said:

2.speaker: beatrice
2.text:
"From that point depends
all heaven and all nature.
Look at the circle joined most close to it—
know that its motion burns so swift
because of the blazing love that spurs it on."

7.speaker: narrator
7.text:
Just as the hemisphere of air remains
splendid and serene when the north wind
blows from his gentler side,
purified and clearing away the haze
that once disturbed it, until the sky laughs
with all the beauties of its pageantry—
so I became, once my Lady
provided me her luminous answer,
and like a star in heaven, the truth appeared.
As soon as her words came to a stop,
those circles blazed and sparkled
exactly like molten iron when it's stirred.
Each spark repeated their coruscation,
and they were so many that their number
makes more millions than the doubling of the chessboard.
I heard them singing "Hosanna" choir by choir
to the fixed point that holds them in their place
and always will, where they have always been.
And she who saw the doubtful meditations
within my mind said:

7.speaker: beatrice
7.text:
"The first circles
have shown you Seraphim and Cherubim.
They follow their bonds with such speed
to become as much like the point as possible,
and they can, as far as they soar high in vision.
Those other Loves that wheel around them
are called Thrones of the divine countenance,
completing the first Triad.
You should know they all find their delight
exactly as far as their vision penetrates
the Truth in which all understanding rests.
From this you see how blessedness
is founded in the power that sees,
not in the power that loves and follows after.
Merit measures this seeing,
born from grace joined with good will—
and so it proceeds from grade to grade.
The second Triad, blossoming
in this eternal spring
that no winter night can strip of leaves,
sings "Hosanna" perpetually
with threefold melody sounding through three
Orders of joy that braid together.
In this hierarchy dwell three Divine orders:
first Dominions, then Virtues,
and third comes the order of Powers.
In the final two dancing rings
Principalities and Archangels wheel,
the last made wholly of Angels at play.
All these orders gaze upward,
and prevail downward with such force
that all draw toward God and all attract.
Dionysius set himself with such great longing
to contemplate these Orders
that he named and ranked them as I do.
But Gregory later disagreed with him,
so when he opened his eyes
within this heaven, he smiled at himself.
And if a mortal revealed so much
secret truth on earth, don't be amazed—
the one who saw it here disclosed it to him,
along with much more truth about these circles."

2.speaker: narrator
2.text:
For as long as the scales of heaven hold the sun and moon
in perfect balance at the zenith,
until both shift hemispheres and tip the equilibrium—
that's how long Beatrice kept silent,
her face lit with a smile,
gazing steadily at the point of light that had overwhelmed me.
Then she began:

2.speaker: beatrice
2.text:
"I will tell you what I know you long to hear,
though you haven't asked.
I have seen it all where every When and Where converges.
Not to gain anything for himself—impossible—
but so his splendor might declare through its radiance: 'I exist.'
In his eternity beyond time,
beyond all boundaries, as it pleased him,
Eternal Love opened into new loves.
He was not lying dormant before this moment—
there was no 'before' or 'after'
when God moved upon these waters.
Matter and Form, separate yet joined,
came into being without flaw,
like three arrows released simultaneously
from a three-stringed bow.
And just as sunlight flashes through glass,
amber, or crystal with no delay
between its arrival and full presence,
so this threefold creation
blazed forth from its Lord all at once,
with no sequence of beginning.
Order was created alongside the substances themselves.
At the summit of the world
were placed those beings of pure action—the angels.
At the bottom, pure potential—raw matter.
In between, potential bound to action
by a bond that can never be broken.
Jerome wrote that angels were created
long ages before the material world,
but this truth appears in many places
written by the Holy Spirit's scribes—
you'll find it if you look carefully.
Even reason glimpses this,
for it makes no sense that the movers of the spheres
would lack their perfection for so long.
Now you know where and when and how
these Loves were created—
three fires of curiosity extinguished in your desire.
Before you could count to twenty,
some of these angels
disrupted the foundation of your elements.
The rest remained and began this art
you see before you, circling with such joy
they never cease their dance.
The fall came through the cursed pride
of that one you saw
crushed beneath the weight of all the world.
But those you see here were humble,
recognizing themselves as made from that goodness
which fitted them for such understanding.
Their vision was lifted higher
by enlightening grace and their own merit,
so their will is complete and unwavering.
Don't doubt this—be certain:
it is worthy to receive this grace
in proportion to how the heart opens to it.
Now in this assembly you can contemplate much
if you gather up my words
without needing further help.
But since on earth, in your schools,
they teach that angels possess
hearing, memory, and will,
I'll say more, so you can see
the pure truth that's muddled down there
by equivocation in such lessons.
These beings, joyful in God's presence,
never turn their gaze away
from the one from whom nothing is hidden.
So their vision is never blocked by new objects,
nor do they need to remember
through interrupted thought.
Yet below, people dream while awake,
some believing they speak truth, others not—
the latter bear greater sin and shame.
You don't follow one path in philosophy;
love of appearances and thinking about them
carries you away.
Even this is tolerated here with less scorn
than when Holy Scripture is set aside
or twisted from its meaning.
They don't consider how much blood it costs
to plant it in the world,
or how much it pleases the one
who stays humbly close to it.
Each strives for show, making up his own ideas,
and preachers expound on these
while the Gospel falls silent.
One claims the moon reversed course
during Christ's Passion, blocking the sun
so light couldn't reach below—
a lie, for the light hid itself willingly,
and this eclipse reached Spaniards and Indians
as well as Jews.
Florence doesn't have as many men named Lapi and Bindi
as there are fables like this
shouted from pulpits year after year.
The lambs who don't know better
return from pasture fed on wind,
and ignorance doesn't excuse the harm.
Christ didn't tell his first followers
'Go preach idle tales to the world,'
but gave them a true foundation.
This rang so clearly from their voices
that in the battle to kindle faith,
they made the Gospel their shields and spears.
Now people go forth with jokes and entertainment to preach,
and if they make the crowd laugh,
their hood swells with pride—nothing more required.
But such a creature nests in that cowl
that if ordinary people saw it,
they'd understand what pardons they trust in—
the source of such great folly on earth
that without proof or testimony
they flock to every indulgence.
This is how Saint Anthony fattens his pig,
along with many others worse than pigs,
paying with counterfeit coin.
But since we've wandered far enough,
turn your eyes back to the straight path
so we can shorten the journey.
This angelic nature multiplies itself
in such numbers that no speech
or mortal imagination can reach so far.
If you note what Daniel revealed,
you'll see that in his thousands
a definite number lies concealed.
The primal light that illuminates all
is received in as many ways
as there are splendors joined with it.
Since affection follows the act of understanding,
love's sweetness burns with varying intensity—
some tepid, others blazing.
Now behold the height and breadth
of eternal power, which has made
so many mirrors of itself where it is broken,
while remaining one as before."

2.speaker: narrator
2.text:
The sixth hour blazes above us, and this world
tilts its shadow nearly flat against the earth,
while the depths of heaven grow so profound
that stars begin to fade from view,
vanishing into the celestial abyss.
As dawn, the radiant servant of the sun, advances,
the sky closes itself to us,
light after light extinguished from our sight.
Just so, the eternal Triumph
that plays forever around the point that conquered me—
seeming enclosed by what it itself encloses—
slowly faded from my vision.
This forced me to turn my eyes back to Beatrice,
my inability to see anything else
and my love both compelling me.
If everything I have said of her until now
could be gathered into a single song of praise,
it would still be inadequate for this moment.
The beauty I beheld not only transcends
our human understanding—I truly believe
only its Creator can fully comprehend it.
I confess myself defeated by this passage
more than any comic or tragic poet
was ever overcome by their most difficult theme.
For as the sun blinds the most sensitive sight,
so the memory of that sweet smile
robs my mind of its very essence.
From the first day I saw her face
in this life until this moment,
my song has never ceased following her—
but now this sequence must end,
unable to pursue her beauty further with my verse,
like any artist reaching the limits of their power.
I leave her to a greater fame
than my trumpet can provide,
as it brings this difficult matter to its close.
With the voice and bearing of a perfect guide,
she began again:

2.speaker: beatrice
2.text:
"We have emerged
from the largest celestial sphere
into the heaven that is pure light—
intellectual light filled with love,
love of true goodness filled with joy,
joy that surpasses every sweetness.
Here you will see both hosts of Paradise,
and one of them in the same form
you will witness at the final judgment."

2.speaker: narrator
2.text:
Like sudden lightning that scatters
the visual spirits, robbing the eye
of its impression of the strongest objects,
so a living light flashed around me,
leaving me wrapped in such a veil
of brilliance that I could see nothing.

3.speaker: dante
3.text: Where is she?"

3.speaker: narrator
3.text: I said at once.

3.speaker: st_bernard
3.text:
"To fulfill your longing, Beatrice sent me from my place.
If you look up to the third circle
of the highest tier, you will see her again
upon the throne her merits have earned.

5.speaker: dante
5.text:
O Lady, in whom my hope is strong,
who for my salvation endured
leaving your footprints in Hell—
of all the things I have seen,
I recognize the power and grace
as coming from your goodness.
You have brought me from slavery to freedom
by every path, every means
by which you had the power to do it.
Keep showing me your magnificence,
so that my soul, which you have healed,
may be released from the body
in a way that pleases you.

6.speaker: narrator
6.text:
So I prayed. And she, so far away,
seemed to smile and looked at me once more,
then turned toward the eternal fountain.
The holy old man said:

6.speaker: st_bernard
6.text:
"So that you may
complete your journey perfectly—
the purpose for which prayer and holy love sent me—
let your eyes fly around this garden,
for seeing it will prepare your sight
to climb higher along the divine ray.
And she, the Queen of Heaven,
for whom I burn completely with love,
will grant us every grace,
because I am her faithful Bernard."

6.speaker: narrator
6.text:
Like someone who perhaps comes from Croatia
to gaze upon our Veronica,
never satisfied by its ancient fame,
but thinks while it is displayed,

7.speaker: narrator
7.text:
My Lord Jesus Christ, true God,
was your face really like this?"—
so was I, gazing at the living love
of the man who in this world,
through contemplation, tasted that peace.

7.speaker: st_bernard
7.text:
"Son of grace, you will not know this joyful life
by keeping your eyes fixed down here
at the bottom.
Look at the circles, even the most distant,
until you see the Queen enthroned
to whom this realm is subject and devoted.

4.speaker: dante
4.text:
Holy father, who for my sake endures
being here below, leaving the sweet place
where you sit by eternal right,
who is that Angel gazing with such joy
into our Queen's eyes,
so enamored he seems made of fire?

5.speaker: narrator
5.text:
So I turned again to the teaching
of him who found delight in Mary
as the morning star delights in sun.
He answered:

5.speaker: st_bernard
5.text:
"All the gallantry and grace
that can exist in Angel and in soul
are his—and we would have it so,
for he carried the palm down to Mary
when God's Son chose
to take our burden on himself.
But follow now with your eyes as I speak
and note the great nobles
of this most just and merciful empire.
Those two sitting highest above,
being closest to the Empress,
are like two roots of this Rose.
He placed near her on the left
is the father whose bold appetite
brought such bitter taste to humankind.
On the right you see that ancient father
of Holy Church, to whom Christ
entrusted the keys of this lovely flower.
Beside him sits the one who saw
all the dark days of that beautiful bride
won with spear and nails before his death.
Next to the other rests that leader
under whom the ungrateful, fickle,
stiff-necked people lived on manna.
Opposite Peter you see Anna,
so content gazing at her daughter
she doesn't move her eyes while singing Hosanna.
Opposite the eldest father of our house
sits Lucy, she who moved your Lady
when you bent your brow to rush downward.
But since the moments of your vision fly,
here we'll stop, like a good tailor
who cuts the coat to fit his cloth.
We'll turn our eyes toward the Primal Love,
so looking on him you may penetrate
as far as possible into his radiance.
But lest perhaps you fall back,
beating wings you think move you forward,
grace must be obtained through prayer—
grace from her who has power to help you.
Follow me with your love
so your heart won't turn from my words."

5.speaker: narrator
5.text: And he began this holy prayer:

1.speaker: st_bernard
1.text:
You are the Virgin Mother, daughter of your own Son,
humble and exalted beyond every other creature,
the destined goal of God's eternal plan.

You are the one who so ennobled human nature
that its Creator did not disdain
to become what He had made.

In your womb was rekindled the love
whose warmth allowed this flower
to bloom in eternal peace.

Here you are for us the noonday torch
of charity, and below among mortals
you are the living fountain of hope.

Lady, you are so great and so powerful
that whoever seeks grace without turning to you
tries to make his desire fly without wings.

2.speaker: st_bernard
2.text:
Your kindness not only helps
those who ask for it,
but often runs ahead of the asking itself.
In you is compassion, in you is mercy,
in you magnificence—in you is gathered
whatever goodness exists in any creature.
Now this man, who from the deepest pit
of the universe to here has witnessed
the spiritual lives one by one,
begs you for grace to gain such power
that he may lift his eyes still higher
toward the ultimate salvation.
And I, who never burned more for my own vision
than I do for his, offer you all my prayers—
and pray they prove sufficient—
that you would scatter from him every cloud
of mortality with your prayers,
so that the Supreme Joy might be revealed to him.
I pray further, Queen, you who can do
whatever you will, that you preserve
his heart's devotion after so great a vision.
Let your protection overcome human frailty.
See how Beatrice and all the blessed ones
clasp their hands together, joining my prayers to you!

2.speaker: narrator
2.text:
The eyes beloved and revered by God,
fixed upon the one who spoke,
showed us how welcome devout prayers are to her.
Then they turned toward the Eternal Light—
that Light on which no creature
could believably focus such a clear gaze.
And I, who was approaching
the end of all desires,
felt the fire of longing within me reach its peak, as it should.
Bernard smiled and gestured for me to look upward,
but I was already doing
exactly what he wanted,
because my sight, becoming purified,
was entering deeper and deeper
into the ray of that High Light which is truth itself.
From that moment on, what I saw
was greater than our language can express—
speech fails before such vision,
and memory surrenders to such overwhelming experience.
Like someone who sees something in a dream,
and after waking the feeling remains
but nothing else returns to mind,
so am I now—my vision has almost entirely
faded away, yet still distilling
in my heart is the sweetness born from it.
So snow melts under the sun's touch,
so the Sibyl's prophecies written on light leaves
were lost upon the wind.
O Supreme Light, you who rise so far
above mortal understanding,
lend back to my mind a little of what you appeared to be,
and give my tongue such power
that it might leave just one spark of your glory
for future generations.
By returning somewhat to my memory
and sounding even faintly in these verses,
more of your victory will be grasped.
I believe the intensity of the living ray
I endured would have overwhelmed me
if I had turned my eyes away from it.
I remember I grew bolder
because of this, so much that I joined
my gaze with the Infinite Glory.
O abundant grace, through which I dared
to fix my sight upon the Eternal Light
until my vision was consumed in it!
In its depths I saw gathered together,
bound by love into a single volume,
everything that is scattered in pages throughout the universe—
substance and accidents and their workings,
all fused together in such a way
that what I'm describing is one simple light.
I believe I saw the universal form
of this great knot,
because as I say this I feel my joy expand.
A single moment brings me more forgetfulness
than twenty-five centuries brought to the voyage
that made Neptune marvel at the Argo's shadow.
My mind, completely suspended this way,
gazed steadfast, motionless, attentive,
and grew more inflamed the more it watched.
In the presence of that light, one becomes such
that it's impossible to ever consent
to turn away from it toward any other sight,
because the good that is the object of the will
is gathered completely there,
and outside it, what is perfect there becomes defective.
My words will fall shorter now
in describing what I still remember
than an infant's whose tongue still seeks the breast.
Not because the living light I gazed upon
contained more than one pure image—
it is always what it was before—
but because my sight grew stronger
by looking, that one appearance
kept transforming as I myself changed.
Within the deep, luminous substance
of the High Light, three circles appeared to me
of three colors but one size,
and one seemed reflected by the second
like rainbow reflected in rainbow,
and the third seemed fire breathed equally from both.
How feeble all speech is, how it falls short
of my conception! And compared to what I saw,
calling this inadequate is not enough.
O Eternal Light, existing in yourself alone,
alone understanding yourself, and understood
by yourself and understanding, you love and smile upon yourself!
That circle which appeared in you
as reflected light,
when my eyes contemplated it awhile,
seemed painted within itself, in its own color,
with our human image—
and so my sight was completely absorbed in it.
Like a mathematician struggling
to square the circle, who cannot discover
through thought the principle he needs,
so was I faced with that new vision.
I wanted to see how the image fit the circle,
how it found its place there,
but my own wings were not sufficient for this—
except that then my mind was struck
by a flash of lightning that fulfilled its wish.
Here my high imagination lost its power,
but already my desire and will were turning,
like a wheel that spins with perfect balance,
moved by the Love that moves the sun and all the stars.
